Interface ChaosControlPlane

All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable
All Known Implementing Classes:
ChaosRuntime, TrackingChaosControlPlane
public interface ChaosControlPlane extends AutoCloseable
Primary entry point to the chaos agent runtime.

A single instance is installed per JVM when the agent attaches, accessible via ChaosPlatform.current() (or ChaosPlatform.installed(), empty while no agent is installed) or installed in test code via ChaosPlatform.installLocally().

Core operations:

  • activate(ChaosScenario) / activate(ChaosPlan) — inject chaos
  • openSession(String) — create an isolated session scope for a single test
  • diagnostics() — inspect scenario states and counters
  • addEventListener(ChaosEventListener) — observe chaos events in real time
  • close() — stop all active scenarios and clean up resources

Thread safety: all methods are thread-safe.

  • Method Details

    • activate

      ChaosActivationHandle activate(ChaosScenario scenario)
      Activates a single chaos scenario at JVM scope.

      The scenario is validated against selector/effect compatibility and registered immediately. Scenarios with ActivationPolicy.StartMode.AUTOMATIC begin intercepting operations instantly. Manual-start scenarios require a subsequent ChaosActivationHandle.start() call.

      The exceptions have no common root besides RuntimeException: catch the ones below, or RuntimeException. Every failure of an open control plane is recorded once in the diagnostics and published as a FAILED event before it is thrown; an activation on a closed one throws IllegalStateException and records nothing.

      Parameters:
      scenario - the scenario to activate; must have ChaosScenario.ScenarioScope.JVM scope
      Returns:
      a handle for lifecycle control; close it to stop the scenario
      Throws:
      ChaosValidationException - if the selector ↔ effect combination is invalid
      ChaosUnsupportedFeatureException - if the scenario requires a JVM feature not available at runtime
      ChaosActivationConflictException - if a scenario with the same ID is still registered or active (a ChaosActivationException)
      ChaosActivationException - if the scenario is SESSION-scoped
      ChaosInstrumentationException - if the instrumentation the scenario needs cannot be woven (a ChaosActivationException)
      IllegalStateException - if the control plane is closed

    • activate

      ChaosActivationHandle activate(ChaosPlan plan)
      Activates all scenarios in a ChaosPlan at JVM scope.

      All scenarios activate atomically: either all succeed or the plan activation fails. The returned handle controls all scenarios in the plan as a group. Every scenario is validated and every hook the plan needs is woven before any scenario is registered.

      The exceptions have no common root besides RuntimeException: catch the ones below, or RuntimeException. Every failure of an open control plane is recorded once in the diagnostics and published as a FAILED event before it is thrown; an activation on a closed one throws IllegalStateException and records nothing.

      Parameters:
      plan - all scenarios must have ChaosScenario.ScenarioScope.JVM scope
      Returns:
      a composite handle that stops all plan scenarios when closed
      Throws:
      ChaosValidationException - if a scenario fails validation
      ChaosUnsupportedFeatureException - if a scenario requires more than the runtime provides
      ChaosActivationConflictException - if a scenario's ID is still registered or active
      ChaosActivationException - if a scenario in the plan is not JVM-scoped
      ChaosInstrumentationException - if the instrumentation the plan needs cannot be woven
      IllegalStateException - if the control plane is closed

    • openSession

      ChaosSession openSession(String displayName)
      Opens a named session scope for per-test chaos isolation.

      Scenarios activated on the returned session affect only threads bound to it: the calling thread, which is bound from this call until ChaosSession.close(), and threads bound with ChaosSession.bind(). Multiple sessions may be active simultaneously without interfering with each other.

      Always close the session when the test completes to stop all session scenarios and release the session scope: 

      try (ChaosSession session = controlPlane.openSession("my-test")) {
    session.activate(scenario);
    // ...
}
      Parameters:
      displayName - human-readable name for this session; appears in diagnostics and logs
      Returns:
      a new session; caller is responsible for closing it
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if displayName is null
      IllegalStateException - if the control plane is closed

    • diagnostics

      ChaosDiagnostics diagnostics()
      Returns the read-only diagnostics view for this control plane instance.

      Use to inspect scenario states, application counters, failure records, and runtime capabilities. The same view is exposed over JMX at com.macstab.chaos.jvm:type=ChaosDiagnostics.

      Returns:
      the diagnostics view for this control plane

    • addEventListener

      void addEventListener(ChaosEventListener listener)
      Registers a listener that receives all chaos lifecycle and application events.

      Listeners are invoked synchronously on the thread that triggers the event. Implementations must be non-blocking and must not throw.

      Common use cases:

      • JFR integration — emit JFR events correlated with chaos activity (built in, installed automatically when jdk.jfr is available)
      • Test assertions — verify that specific scenarios fired during a test run
      • Custom metrics — bridge chaos events to Micrometer, Prometheus, or similar
      Parameters:
      listener - a non-null, non-blocking listener; must not throw from onEvent

    • removeEventListener

      boolean removeEventListener(ChaosEventListener listener)
      Removes a listener registered with addEventListener(ChaosEventListener); a listener registered more than once is removed once. Removing an asynchronous listener stops its delivery thread; events still queued for it are discarded.
      Parameters:
      listener - the listener to remove, as it was registered
      Returns:
      true if it was registered

    • close

      void close()
      Stops and removes every scenario, those of open sessions included, cleans up stressor resources and closes the listeners that are AutoCloseable.

      After this call the control plane is inert; all selector evaluations return no-match. An open session stays open but activates nothing more (its activate fails with IllegalStateException); its own ChaosSession.close() still ends its binding of the thread that opened it. Calling close() more than once is safe.

      The JVM-wide control plane the agent installed (ChaosPlatform.installLocally(), current()) cannot be closed: other tests, framework integrations and the management endpoints share it.

      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if this is the JVM-wide control plane of ChaosPlatform

    • bindSession

      ChaosSession.ScopeBinding bindSession(@Nullable String sessionId)
      Binds the calling thread to the open session with sessionId, as ChaosSession.bind() would: how a server joins the session a request came from (ChaosSession.HEADER). The id decides for the binding's lifetime: an unknown or closed id runs the thread outside any session, even one it inherited (a pooled server thread started while a test's session was bound).
      Parameters:
      sessionId - the session id, e.g. the value of the ChaosSession.HEADER header; null (no header) also runs the thread outside any session
      Returns:
      the binding to close when the work is done
